title: B199 — mother runs out of memory overnight and stalls (CI killed, node NotReady)
description:
## Why

mother (the only k3s node) stalls for 1–5 minutes several times a night. During a stall it answers nothing: node-exporter misses scrapes, the Woodpecker agents lose gRPC keepalive to the server (and the kubelet/agents lose the API server, `http2: client connection lost`), the server expires the running CI task and the pipeline shows **killed**, and on 2026-09-30 06:44Z the node went `NodeNotReady` (taint-manager eviction started, then cancelled).

Found 2026-09-30 while running CI for B180: pipelines 206, 207, 208 (nightly-images) and 209 all died this way, none on a code verdict. Earlier kills with the same server log (`queue: resubmitting expired task` → `task expired`): pipelines 169, 170 (09-24), 186 (09-25), 191 (09-26). Every failed nightly-images run and most killed pipelines sit in 00:00–03:00 NY.

**Evidence (Prometheus, node-exporter** `192.168.1.243:9100`**, 2026-09-30):**

| UTC | MemAvailable | load1 | note |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 04:58 | 1.66 GB | 14 | minutes before |
| 04:59–05:04 | no samples | — | scrape gap = node frozen; CI 207 + nightly-images killed |
| 05:01 | 1.60 GB | **454** |  |
| 05:04 | 2.75 GB | **589** | recovering |
| 05:10 | 4.9 GB | 9 | normal |

IO stall stays about 5% and CPU wait about 0.2 throughout: this is **memory exhaustion** (reclaim stalls everything into D-state), not disk or CPU. mother has 78 Gi, no swap, and a \~69 Gi always-on baseline (`docs/runbooks/node-capacity.md`); MemAvailable sits at 2.5–4.5 GB **before** the spikes, so any overnight job plus a CI run tips it over.

## Scope

1. **Attribute the spikes.** For each stall (04:05Z, 05:00Z, 06:44Z on 09-30, plus 09-24/25/26), list the top memory consumers from `container_memory_working_set_bytes` (by pod) in the 10 minutes before: which scheduled job (`feast_materialize` 00:05, docker/image prune 00:10/00:15, `timeseries` 00:20, the 01:00 nightly-images build, the 02:17 `weyland_ingestion_job`, 02:30 restic write to MinIO) and which CI step pod (4Gi limits: build, sonar-gate) was running.
2. **Fix the cause** from that attribution — candidates, none chosen yet: stagger or cap the colliding jobs, lower CI step memory, keep full CI out of the pre-dawn window, park idle Tier-2 stores (the documented lever), or raise mother's RAM toward the \~80 Gi host ceiling.
3. **An alert that sees it.** A rule on `node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes` (and a scrape-gap / `up==0` on node-exporter for mother) that fires before the node stalls, plus a Woodpecker "pipeline killed by task expiry" signal so a killed CI run is not read as a cancellation.

## Technical context

| Where | What | Role |
| -- | -- | -- |
| mother (VM 101 on weyland) | 78 Gi RAM, no swap, single k3s node | the stalling node |
| k8s `woodpecker` ns | `woodpecker-server-0`, `woodpecker-agent-{0,1}` (StatefulSets), step pods `wp-*` | server expires tasks when agent keepalive fails |
| repo | `docs/schedules.md` | overnight job timetable to correlate with |
| repo | `docs/runbooks/node-capacity.md`, `docs/runbooks/node-memory-resilience.md` | RAM ceiling, kubelet reserves / eviction-hard |
| repo | `nodes/mother/host/rancher/k3s/config.yaml` | kubelet `system-reserved` / `eviction-hard` |
| repo | `.woodpecker.yml` | step memory limits (build / sonar-gate 4Gi) |
| Prometheus | `node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes`, `node_load1`, `node_pressure_*`, `container_memory_working_set_bytes` | evidence + future alert |

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each listed stall is attributed to named pods/jobs with their memory, recorded in the issue and `docs/runbooks/node-capacity.md`.
- [ ] After the fix, 7 consecutive nights with no node-exporter scrape gap on mother, no `NodeNotReady`, and no Woodpecker `task expired` in the server log.
- [ ] A full CI pipeline started at 01:00 NY completes (drill), or full CI is documented and enforced as daytime-only with the reason.
- [ ] A PrometheusRule fires when mother's MemAvailable stays under a set floor for 2 minutes, proven by a promtool unit test; it reaches Telegram.

## Edge cases & failure modes

* A stall stops node-exporter itself, so an alert on MemAvailable alone can miss the stall; the scrape-gap/`up` rule covers that.
* Evictions under pressure can kill a Dagster run mid-write; the fix must not trade CI kills for data-job kills.
* Raising RAM past \~80 Gi risks the swapless Proxmox host (91 Gi usable) itself.

## Out of scope

* Moving workloads to the Strix Halo (B134) — that is the long-term relief; this issue makes the single node stable now.
* The B180 work that surfaced it.

Relates B180 ([EMA-238](https://linear.app/emangini/issue/EMA-238/b180-track-host-systemd-units-mother-rogueone-weyland-in-a-yaml-sot)), B134, B123. Detail: docs/backlog.md B199.
